::: {.lead}
Today an AI assistant helps you in Excel, and you check every answer. Each
experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in the AI assistant and Excel on
the lab computer. **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson:
on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step,
write your result in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the
table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel, a browser and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com`), and
  the start file of Lecture 13.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Excel.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · Ask an AI for a formula, then test it

**The idea:** an AI tool can write a formula for you. Tell it three things:
**where** the data is, **which column** holds what, and **what** you want.
Then **test every formula**: check one small result by hand. An AI can use
a wrong column, and the number still looks normal.

**Aim:** get a formula from AI, and test it by hand.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Excel)**
:::

1. Open `sales-start.xlsx`, sheet **Sales** (10 sales, 200 JD in all). Ask
   the AI: *My data is in A1:E11 of an Excel sheet. Column E is the Total
   in JD. Write one formula for the average Total.* Type its formula in
   E13. Check it by hand: 200 ÷ 10.

   {{< record "The formula … ; E13 shows … ; by hand …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **=AVERAGE(E2:E11)**, and E13 shows **20**: by hand, 200 ÷ 10 = 20. The
   formula is right. If the AI gives another range or column, fix it.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="20" unit="JD" hint="The 10 totals add up to 200."}
   The 10 totals of the sheet Sales add up to 200 JD. What must
   `=AVERAGE(E2:E11)` show?

   Why: 200 ÷ 10 = 20 JD: one small calculation by hand tests the formula.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-07/sims/ai-formula-lab.html" poster="../../week-07/sims/ai-formula-lab.png" title="AI Formula Lab: ask for a formula, then test it" >}}

2. In **AI Formula Lab**, do the three jobs. Test each formula by hand. In
   Job 3, what was wrong with the AI's formula?

   {{< record "Job 3: the AI's formula used … ; the right result …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI used **column D** (the quantities) instead of **E** (the totals).
   The fixed formula **=AVERAGE(E2:E11)** gives **18.50 JD** (185 ÷ 10).
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   An AI formula uses the wrong column. What do you see in the cell?

   - [x] a normal-looking number that is wrong

     Why: Excel calculates the wrong column without an error, so you test the result by hand.

   - [ ] an error like #NAME?

     Why: The formula has no wrong name, so Excel shows a number.

   - [ ] an empty cell

     Why: The wrong column has numbers too, so the cell shows a result.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Clean the data with AI advice

**The idea:** data from paper or from many people is often **messy**: rows
typed twice, extra spaces, "drinks" and "Drinks", "9 JD" as text. Messy
data gives wrong results: a filter misses rows, and SUM skips text. An AI
tool can list the steps to clean it; **you** check each step before you do
it. The tools: **Data › Remove Duplicates**, **=TRIM** for spaces, **Find
and Replace** for spellings, numbers without "JD". Never delete real rows
because an AI says so.

**Aim:** clean a messy list, with AI advice that you check.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Excel and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. On a new sheet, type this list from a paper notebook, **with its
   mistakes**: **Item, Type, Total**; **Pen, Paper, 20**; **Juice, drinks,
   12**; **Bag, Bags, 30**; **Bag, Bags, 30**; **Water, Drinks, 9 JD**;
   **Notebook, PAPER, 16**. Ask the AI: *My Excel list has the columns
   Item, Type and Total. One row is typed twice, some types are spelled in
   different ways, and one total is "9 JD". How do I clean it in Excel?
   Give short steps.*

   {{< record "Two steps that the AI gave" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Good steps, for example: **Data › Remove Duplicates** for the bag typed
   twice; write each type the same way (**Find and Replace**, or type
   *Drinks* and *Paper*); type **9** instead of *9 JD*. Check each step: a
   step that deletes real sales is wrong.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   The AI gives five steps. Follow them or not? Sort them.

   Follow it
   :   Remove the row that is typed twice.

       Why: The same sale must count once.

   :   Write drinks and Drinks the same way.

       Why: Then a filter finds all the drinks.

   :   Type 9 instead of 9 JD.

       Why: SUM skips text, so the total must be a number.

   Do not follow it
   :   Delete all the totals under 12.

       Why: They are real sales: never delete real rows.

   :   Delete the column Type.

       Why: You need the types to filter and to chart.
   :::

2. Clean the list: remove the row typed twice (Data › Remove Duplicates),
   write *Drinks* and *Paper* the same way in every row, and type **9**
   for *9 JD*. Then add the totals with **=SUM**.

   {{< record "Rows after cleaning … ; SUM …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **5 rows** stay (the bag counts once), and the SUM is **87 JD** (20 +
   12 + 30 + 9 + 16). Before cleaning, SUM gave 108: it counted the bag
   twice and skipped the text *9 JD*.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="87" unit="JD" hint="20 + 12 + 30 + 9 + 16: the bag counts once."}
   After cleaning, what does SUM give for the five totals?

   Why: 20 + 12 + 30 + 9 + 16 = 87 JD. The bag counts once, and 9 is now a number.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-07/sims/clean-data-lab.html" poster="../../week-07/sims/clean-data-lab.png" title="Clean Data Lab: tidy the sales list with AI advice" >}}

3. In **Clean Data Lab**, use the AI's steps one by one, but check each
   one. Which step do you **not** use? What is the SUM of the clean list?

   {{< record "The bad step … ; the SUM …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Step 6, "Delete Totals under 12"**: it deletes real sales. With the
   other five steps, the clean list adds up to **185 JD**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which AI step in Clean Data Lab is a bad idea?

   - [x] Delete the Totals under 12.

     Why: They are real sales: never delete real rows because an AI says so.

   - [ ] Remove the duplicate rows.

     Why: A row typed twice must count once.

   - [ ] TRIM the extra spaces.

     Why: Extra spaces make the same word look different.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Check the AI's chart advice

**The idea:** an AI can suggest a chart and a title, but its advice is not
always right. Check it with the rule of Lecture 13: **compare** amounts →
column chart; **change over time** → line chart; **parts of one whole** →
pie chart. Make the chart from the **clean** data, and give it a real
title, never "Chart 1".

**Aim:** check the AI's chart advice, and make the right chart.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Excel)**
:::

1. Ask the AI: *Which chart shows how the sales of a shop change from
   Sunday to Thursday?* Then, on the sheet **Days** of `sales-start.xlsx`,
   select **A1:B6** and make the chart that the rule gives. Give it a real
   title.

   {{< record "The AI advised … ; I made a … chart with the title …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A **line chart**: a line shows a change over time. Many AI answers say
   so, but some advise a pie or a column chart: the rule decides. A real
   title, for example "Sales from Sunday to Thursday (JD)".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why is a line chart right for the sales from Sunday to Thursday?

   - [x] It shows a change over time.

     Why: The days follow each other: a line shows up and down.

   - [ ] It shows the parts of one whole.

     Why: That is a pie chart.

   - [ ] It compares types of products.

     Why: The question is about days, not types.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-07/sims/chart-lab.html" poster="../../week-07/sims/chart-lab.png" title="Chart Lab: the right chart for the question" >}}

2. In **Chart Lab**, a weak AI answer advises a **pie chart of the sales
   per day**. Try it, read what the lab says, then make the right chart.

   {{< record "Chart Lab says … ; the right chart …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A pie of the days does not show the change from day to day. The right
   chart for the days is a **line chart**; a pie is only for the parts of
   one whole, like the types of the week.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI suggests the title "Chart 1". What do you write?

   - [x] what the chart shows, for example "Sales per day (JD)"

     Why: A real title says what the chart shows.

   - [ ] "Chart 1", because the AI suggested it

     Why: It says nothing about the numbers.

   - [ ] no title

     Why: Every chart needs a real title.
   :::
